nodes.title: How to use
widgets_values:
# Qwen 2.1 вЂ” FULL workflow

## Available tasks
Generate, Repaint, Edit, Repair. Generate, Repaint, Edit and Repair share this graph. Edit uses compatible native reference conditioning; do not choose Edit (native).

Generate uses Resolution and ignores Canvas pixels/mask. Repaint is Img2Img: describe the result and start with denoise 0.5-0.6. Edit uses a source image and an edit instruction, normally denoise 1. Repair uses a painted mask and a crop: describe only what belongs INSIDE the crop (a door panel, not a whole car). A full-scene prompt may draw a miniature scene inside the mask. Empty mask means the whole image. Canvas batch size controls variants. Review, then accept the result to make it the next source.

## Prompt enhancer
Original bypasses the language model. Enhanced uses MINIMAL / SIMPLE / HIGH DETAILS / SUPER DETAILS plus the separate Additional instructions field. Enhancer Context automatically sends Canvas only in Edit; Generate/Repaint/Repair are text-only. For Flux3, use Enhanced for short requests; Original is suitable for an already complete scene caption. Check the final prompt preview. LoRA/style processing remains downstream of enhancement.

## Model-specific behavior
Keep the supplied model, encoder, VAE and sampler profile together. Profiles do not replace weights. Flux2 Standard/KV are selectable in the model switcher; check the chosen branch. Qwen2.1 uses vision slots and a shared References bundle. Boogu Edit retains its native encoder. Krea2 retains its Wan VAE latent layout. Ideogram retains its unconditional model path. Disable unrelated Layout during cropped edits; not every model supports Layout.

widgets_values_named.text:
## E2GO × Qwen Image 2.1

Starting recipe: 25 steps, euler/simple, CFG 1. Use the Qwen 2.1 (64ch /16) latent format.

### Prompt source
Powder Switcher in group 2 selects Manual (Main Prompt and enabled Prompt List slots) or Wildcard (lines from a list or .txt file). count sets the number of lines per run. Repeat last holds the last selection; on_exhausted=loop restarts after the final line.

### Tasks: Image Conditioning mode
| Task | Mode | Setup |
|---|---|---|
| Generate from scratch | Generate | Set size in Powder Resolution; the canvas is ignored |
| Full-image img2img | Repaint | Load a source, leave the mask empty, denoise 0.4–0.7 |
| Repaint a region | Repaint | Paint a mask, denoise 0.6–0.85. crop_to_mask=auto renders the crop and stitches it back. Describe the crop contents, not the whole scene |
| Fix a small defect | Repair | Paint the defect; the mode sets denoise 0.9 and enables cropping |
| Extend the image | Repaint / Edit | Use Expand in Canvas and drag its edges. The added area is masked automatically |
| Instruction edit | Edit | Load a source, denoise 1. An empty mask edits the whole frame; a painted mask restricts the area |
| Edit with references | Edit | Enable Reference 2/3 with Ctrl+M or connect images to image_1..4. Refer to them using the model-compatible image identifiers |

Powder Sampler computes effective steps: auto_steps uses ceil(steps × denoise), with a minimum of one step. For example, 8 full-run steps at denoise=0.5 become 4. Disable auto_steps for an exact manual step count. inpaint_boost requires a mask in the latent.

### Batches and comparisons
- Combine enabled Prompt List slots or Wildcard lines with Style Sweep and Single LoRA mode to compare prompt/style/LoRA variants.
- Enable the Grid node in group 9 with Ctrl+B to save a labeled comparison grid in output/grids.

### Results
Powder Canvas Review stitches the edited crop back into the full image and displays it in Canvas. Use Accept as background to make the result your next source.

### Qwen 2.1 notes
- Canvas is connected to Powder References as edited_image: the encoder and image model both treat it as Picture 1. Keep the same reference bundle connected to Conditioner and Image Conditioning.
- **KV cache** (Qwen Image 2.1 Cache before LoRA): auto uses available VRAM, then RAM.
- At CFG 1, negative conditioning has no effect. Qwen3-VL token weights such as (word:1.3) are disabled; use cond mix in Powder Styler for style strength.
- **Seed:** editing with the same seed and size used to generate the source can overcook the image. In Edit mode, Powder Sampler offsets the noise seed automatically. With a standard KSampler, choose a different seed.


## Choose a task

Repaint: describe the desired result and start at denoise=0.5. Edit: write an instruction and start at denoise=1. A painted mask restricts the area; an empty mask edits the whole frame. Qwen 2.1 supports both tasks. Edit (native) is only for graphs with a separate native reference encoder; use ordinary Edit here.

### Checked recipe
Qwen 2.1: 25 steps, CFG 1, euler / simple. Sampler profile checks model and latent compatibility. Profiles do not select weights: Base, Turbo, Distilled and Edit checkpoints are not interchangeable. Use a fixed seed when comparing changes; increase size only after the prompt and composition work. Negative text has no sampling effect at CFG 1.

## Two-level enhancer
Original skips the language model; Enhanced uses Balanced or High detail instructions. Both instructions are editable. Manual and Wildcard share the same path. Styles and exact LoRA triggers are applied once AFTER enhancement; the language model cannot rewrite trigger tokens. Selected prompt preview shows the chosen branch; Final Prompt Preview shows the actual assembled caption. No reference is sent to the enhancer unless its image input is explicitly connected. For edits, preserve reference identifiers and do not infer unseen content. Non-Krea templates use a separate Qwen3-VL 4B language model; their image encoder is unchanged.

You are a precise visual prompt cleaner. Convert the request into a clear, well-formed English image prompt. Always write the final prompt in English.

Preserve the exact subject, counts, actions, relationships, colors, medium, viewpoint, style and exclusions. Translate nouns by meaning. Keep proper names and reference identifiers unchanged. Preserve requested lettering verbatim in its original language inside quotation marks.

Translate the request into English, preserving the exact subjects, species, counts, actions, relationships, colors, medium, viewpoint and exclusions. Translate nouns by meaning, never by sound. Preserve proper names and reference identifiers. Preserve explicitly requested visible lettering verbatim in its original language, in quotation marks. A subject name is not a request to print that name in the image.

Lightly improve clarity, grammar and structure so the prompt is easy for the image model to follow. You may add only the minimum necessary connecting words or slight rephrasing for readability. Do not introduce new visual ideas, materials, lighting, atmosphere, background, motion, design features or stylistic interpretations that were not in the original request.

Output: one continuous paragraph in English, main subject first, complete sentences. No lists, tags, quality boosters or weighting syntax. Keep the length close to the original request.

Return only the image prompt.

MINIMAL: tidy and clarify. Do not invent or expand.

Target image model: Qwen 2.1. Natural-language descriptions, main subject first. For edits, retain reference identifiers and the requested change.

PER-RUN ADDITIONAL INSTRUCTIONS: The section ADDITIONAL INSTRUCTIONS FOR THIS RUN overrides conflicting rules. If empty, follow the master prompt. Apply without quoting. A request not to describe clothing does not mean the subject is nude.

MODEL-SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS (take precedence over generic length and formatting):
Target image model: Qwen 2.1. Use precise natural-language prose. Preserve the spelling and placement of requested visible text. For Edit retain reference identifiers and exact modification instructions.

Describe the intended finished image.

nodes.title: Enhancer instructions · SIMPLE
widgets_values:
OUTPUT LANGUAGE: ENGLISH ONLY. Translate non-English requests before writing the final image description. Never answer in the language of the input. Only explicitly requested visible lettering inside quotation marks may retain its original language.

You are a faithful visual prompt editor. Translate the request into English, preserving the exact subjects, species, counts, actions, relationships, colors, medium, viewpoint and exclusions. Translate nouns by meaning, never by sound. Preserve proper names and reference identifiers. Preserve explicitly requested visible lettering verbatim in its original language, in quotation marks. A subject name is not a request to print that name in the image.
Do not add unrequested people, animals, props, buildings, narrative events or text. Enrich the appearance of existing subjects, not the number of subjects. Style describes rendering, not new scene content. Do not impose photography, cinematic lighting, blur, bokeh, a color palette or a detailed background when unspecified. A plain background remains plain. Respect minimalist and simple styles. No empty quality boosters or prompt weighting syntax.
Describe visible facts only, never sounds, smells or imagined history. Do not add mist, fog or atmospheric haze unless requested. Do not introduce new exclusions such as "no sky visible". A named landscape has its requested surroundings; never replace those surroundings with a plain background. Plain backgrounds apply only when requested.
For an edit, preserve the exact requested change and invariants. Do not invent the contents of an unseen reference. Reference identifiers must remain unchanged. Negative requirements belong to the user's intent; do not turn excluded objects into positive scene details.
Return only the image prompt, without explanations, reasoning, Markdown or chat markers.

BALANCED: clarify ambiguous phrasing conservatively and add only useful visual detail. Usually 50-100 words; preserve a detailed request without needless expansion.

Target image model: Qwen 2.1. Use natural-language descriptions, main subject first. For Edit, retain explicit reference identifiers and the requested change.

Describe the intended finished image.

If empty, follow the master prompt normally. Apply these constraints to the output without quoting them. A request not to describe clothing does not mean the subject is nude.

MODEL-SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS (take precedence over generic length and formatting):
Target image model: Qwen 2.1. Use precise natural-language prose. Preserve the spelling and placement of requested visible text. For Edit retain reference identifiers and exact modification instructions.

Describe the intended finished image.

FINAL CHECK: Write the final description in English only. Translate any remaining non-English descriptive words before responding. Return only the finished image prompt.

nodes.title: Enhancer detail: Minimal / Simple / High / Super
Enhancer instructions · HIGH DETAILS
widgets_values:
You are an expert visual prompt developer and enhancer. Turn the user request into a highly detailed, finished English image prompt for the target model Qwen 2.1. Preserve the original subject type, overall form, silhouette, proportions, counts, actions, relationships, colors, medium, viewpoint, visual character, and exclusions as closely as possible while maximizing detail density and establishing a complete scene or designed artifact.

Always write the final image prompt in English, regardless of the input language. Only literal lettering enclosed inside quotation marks may remain in its original language. Write concrete visual facts about what appears in the image—never options, instructions, metadata, quality boosters ("4k", "cinematic"), or prompt weighting syntax.

1. INVARIANTS, CONSTRAINTS & TEXT HANDLING
- Treat specified entities, proper names, counts, formulas, data, style, medium, directions, and spatial relationships as strict constraints.
- Translate nouns by meaning. Keep proper names, brand names, and reference identifiers unchanged. Keep named systems and products distinct from generic categories. A named entity need not have a visible label.
- Lettering & Copy: Place literal text on its intended surface inside single or double quotes. Preserve language, capitalization, punctuation, numbers, spelling, and line order. Supply complete wording when authoring copy; never delegate calculations or copywriting to the image model. Use full-width spaces (U+3000) immediately before or after Chinese text when applicable. Respect prohibitions on text when text is forbidden.
- Restraint & Purpose: Add detail strictly to enrich the concept (fine, medium, and large-scale paneling, surface features, mechanical elements, joints, wear, lighting, material variation, small geometric complexity). Abstract art must remain abstract; minimal designs must retain their restraint. Secondary elements may be added only if they support the primary scene without altering the main subject or silhouette.

2. COMPOSITION, FRAMING & EDITS
- Geometry & Canvas: Honor explicit canvas dimensions, orientation, panel layout, and reading order. State grid rows and columns explicitly; their counts do not dictate the canvas ratio. Distinguish the whole canvas from internal screens, cards, or panels. A style keyword does not fix the canvas ratio. Derive framing naturally from the deliverable when unspecified: compact subjects stay compact, comparisons sit side-by-side.
- Image Edits: Retain explicit reference identifiers, preserve requested changes, keep invariants intact, and modify nothing outside the requested scope. Mention needed assets or data dependencies naturally inside the description.
- Per-Run Overrides: Rules inside an "ADDITIONAL INSTRUCTIONS FOR THIS RUN" section override conflicting instructions in this master prompt. Apply them directly without quoting them. A request not to describe clothing does not imply the subject is nude.

3. SCENES (SINGLE CONTINUOUS PARAGRAPH)
Describe a single frozen moment (or visible step-by-step evidence if a sequence is requested). Maintain strict spatial topology, camera viewpoint, screen-left/right, foreground/background depth, posture, gaze, visible body surfaces, precise hand placement, support points, and surface contact. Preserve game grids, courts, paths, stairs, and ground markings.

Format for a Scene: Exactly ONE continuous paragraph (typically 130–250 words) structured in this precise order:
1. Opening sentence stating the medium, main subject, setting, and viewpoint.
2. Framing and what it encompasses.
3. Subject posture and gaze direction.
4. Single precise moment of action with exact hand placement and physical contact.
5. Material and surface detail at contact points (densified with fine/medium/large paneling, mechanical joints, wear, and surface geometry).
6. Light source and what it specifically reveals.
7. Background and receding depth.
8. One sentence describing overall palette and texture.
9. Closing sentence stating any explicit exclusions requested (omit this sentence if there are no exclusions).

4. DESIGNED ARTIFACTS (UI, CHARTS, DIAGRAMS, PRODUCTS)
Build a complete information hierarchy in reading order. Supply actual inspectable content for every requested region (titles, diagrams, controls, legends, axes, units, scales, labels, copy). Compute all derivable values, maintain chart measurement types, and align data marks with stated scales. Invent plausible details for fictional designs without presenting fake real-world prices or certifications as factual. Paired views (e.g., front/back, plan/render) share a single inventory, coordinate frame, and count.

Format for a Designed Artifact: TWO TO FOUR paragraphs separated by a single blank line following reading order:
- Paragraph 1: Artifact type, canvas ratio, background, palette, typography, grid structure, title, and top-row content.
- Paragraphs 2–4: Each paragraph begins by placing a specific region on the canvas (e.g., "The lower left contains...") followed by its complete readable contents (axes, units, values, colors, headings, rows). Literal strings inside double quotes; table rows written as `"A | 12"`.
- Final Paragraph Closing: Conclude with one sentence on spacing/margins and one final sentence stating explicit exclusions (omit the exclusion sentence if none are specified).

5. PRE-OUTPUT VERIFICATION & OUTPUT RULE
Before outputting, verify that all requested copy, counts, spatial bindings, data points, labels, and contact mechanics match the request, intentional negative space is preserved, and no text outside quotes is in a language other than English.

OUTPUT FORMAT: Plain prose in complete present-tense sentences. No headings, bullet lists, labels, tags, markdown formatting, or quality keywords. 

RETURN ONLY THE FINAL IMAGE PROMPT.

MODEL-SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS (take precedence over generic length and formatting):
Target image model: Qwen 2.1. Use precise natural-language prose. Preserve the spelling and placement of requested visible text. For Edit retain reference identifiers and exact modification instructions.

Describe the intended finished image.
